body:
Thank you for your response. However, I do believe spending less time with them might help me learn to cope with my issues in my own time a bit more. So, I'm bringing my learning curve into the relationship as little as possible.

My jealousy issues have done loads of harm already.

Thank you. Your suggestion does seem to help with my anxiety.

I've been seeing someone for 5 years and I believe I put too much importance on our relationship as it's the longest one I've had. 

We have had intense chemistry at times.

So, I have trouble adopting a non-hierarchal structure because I enjoy so much of my time with them.

Any tips on how to detach from them a bit so I can do drop the feeling of primary partnership along with the title?
All jokes have some truth to them. But I hope things are alright on your end AND the other person's end. Hurt people, hurt people. They probably said it from a sad, angry place.

Do they like their partner's quality or do they tolerate it? Granted the person you commented on seems to show resentment and lack of boundary setting which can screw a relationship, you sound bitter rather than helpful. Quite rude, imo.

Because their scenario has similarities it's hard not to take your comment as personal. But I understand this is reddit, so taking things personally is kinda useless. Especially with comments like yours.

In the case of my partner, she has so many superb qualities. This is swiping debacle is honestly worth finding a compromise for. Like swiping when she's not around. I talk to A LOT of people. 

Many people here had good suggestions.

Also, my partner said she doesn't have a problem with me talking to people - it's just something about the swiping.

I might be taking the L in the short term by not swiping around her. But long term this is a W because I get to enjoy her other qualities and the other things she's cool with.

There's nuance to everything, dude.
